title: Research sprint goal: The landing lock is fair, a code item lands in one run, and claims and dead runs do not block
goal: The sprint goal's open questions are answered with the kb tools first and the live docs for the gaps, and the findings are written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills, so each committed item can name the knowledge it needs. Tested rows for kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv are a code-lane path (_tools/kblane.py): a story finished with them lands through backlog.py land ID --wait-merge SECONDS, not done --commit.
notes: No outside facts: the sprint's questions concern this repository's own land, claim and monitoring tools, so no official source or live doc applies. Baseline the sprint's review compares against, measured 2026-11-09 from backlog.py's ops rows (bl_stall.ops_rows, this host's spool and the committed sidecars) for 2026-11-08 18:00 to 2026-11-09 13:00 CET (17:00Z to 12:00Z; first row 17:05Z, last 11:51Z): 325 land.end rows, 282 exit 0, 43 non-zero. Refused at step landing lock: 13 land runs of 10 items, each a land.end with exit 1 and no step row, after 1807 to 1811 s of waiting (the bound is 1800 s); 3 other stops with no step row (ST-hojylkmb after 0.6 s and 5.6 s, ST-a73x2hvh after 215 s). Land time: 309 passes ran steps, 17.9 h from each pass's first step start to its land.end, in a 19 h window, median 100 s per pass; that includes the wait for the merge request where a pass has a wait-merge step (28 in the window, 1 of them failed). Passes per code item: 146 land.end rows carry lane=code and 129 of those items ran another stepped pass after it: the first passes took 4.4 h in all (median 90 s) and the later passes 9.5 h (median 99 s), a second run started by hand; the rows do not say whether the first pass ended on the missing code branch (BG-ot47avdg). Failed land.end rows by last step before them: 16 with none (13 lock, 3 other), siblings 7, stale 6, checks 5, kbgit.py-sync-push 3, verify 2, fetch 2, rebase 1, done 1. Command to repeat it: python3 -c over bl_stall.ops_rows('.') grouped by item, event land.step and land.end, as above. The review reruns it for the window of the sprint's own landings; fewer than 13 lock refusals per night and one stepped pass per code item are the goals' own measures.
